question: The Commission recently published a regulation introducing provisional anti-dumping duties on imports of polyamide yarn from China1, after concluding that China was selling polyamide yarn on the EU market below fair market value, causing material injury. This action, while dealing with one problem, exacerbates issues for European producers in the knitting, weaving and light industry sectors.

Introducing anti-dumping duties on polyamide yarn – essential for manufacturing – without addressing the issue of finished products, reduces EU competitiveness, shifts production out of the EU and puts enormous pressure on small and medium-sized enterprises, which form the cornerstone of the EU economy.
The fate of around 100 manufacturers employing a large number of people from central and eastern Europe, including Poland, has been left hanging in the balance. In the light of the above: 1.
Did the Commission evaluate the impact of anti-dumping duties on EU manufacturers prior to imposing the duties?
Is the Commission considering anti-dumping duties on finished products from China in order to level the playing field for downstream manufacturing in the EU?

How is the current situation consistent with the EU’s broader objectives of supporting reindustrialisation, preserving manufacturing capacity and protecting employment within its light industry sector?

Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/734 of 26 March 2026 imposing a provisional antidumping duty on imports of yarns of polyamide originating in the People’s Republic of China (OJ L, 2026/734, 27.3.2026, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2026/734/oj). 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.7.2026) The impact of anti-dumping measures on the downstream industries is analysed in the context of the EU interest analysis. However, this requires cooperation of the users of polyamide yarns. Upon initiation, 140 users of polyamide yarns identified in the complaint were invited to cooperate. Only three users and one users’ association registered as interested parties.

None of them filled in the user questionnaire, but merely provided general comments on the possible negative impact of the measures on the downstream industry, not supported by any evidence or data. In case the downstream industry faces pressure from unfairly priced imports, it can also submit a complaint and request an anti-dumping investigation.

In order for the investigation to be initiated, the complaint should contain sufficient evidence of dumping, injury and the causal link between the two. The current investigation has the objective of preserving manufacturing capacity and protecting employment of the yarn industry (being a part of light industry sector), which is directly endangered by unfair dumped imports from China.

The Commission will monitor potential changes in the pattern of trade after imposition of anti-dumping duties should the Chinese exporters move their export activity to the downstream industry that is using polyamide yarns.
